text:
Connor Bedard had shoulder surgery and is out four months, ESPN's estimated return March 23. For a Blackhawks team already near the bottom, it's the injury that turns a hard season into, as one reporter put it, a lost one. He had 18 points in 15 games. In the three games since, Ryan Donato has taken his spot beside Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi, and Frank Nazar's ice time has climbed from about 18 minutes a night to almost 22.

What's strange is how lively the Hawks have looked in the meantime. They're 3-1-1 in their last five and won 6-3 in Vancouver on Sunday behind Kantserov's hat trick. Nazar has seven goals in a six-game point streak (hot, our numbers say, on some bounces), Patrick Kane has a five-game streak of his own, and rookie defenseman Sam Rinzel just joined Bobby Orr, Borje Salming and Gordie Howe as the only defensemen with five straight multi-assist games. The season-long picture is still grim: 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), a -31 goal difference, and 0.3% playoff odds. Spencer Knight is at -1.9 saved above expected. Our sleepers are both Hawks: Donato at 17% to score and Nazar at 58% for a point.

Seattle's young story is Berkly Catton, who scored the first hat trick of his NHL career against Vancouver and has 9 points in ten games, though our numbers say some of that is fortune. Matty Beniers has goals in three straight and moved onto the first power-play unit with Jared McCann out until around Jan. 2. Bobby McMann is the opposite case: no goals in 14 games on 2.9 expected. Frederick Gaudreau plays his 500th NHL game. Philipp Grubauer, at +0.2, is projected in goal.

Neither team wins the chance battle often (Seattle takes 45% at five on five, Chicago 44%), and our numbers have the Kraken at 3.21 expected goals to Chicago's 2.77. First meeting of the season.
headline: The Blackhawks without Bedard, and Catton's hat-trick glow in Seattle
